statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Mandatory use of French language and Latin script; no foreign-language names or transliterations permitted
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names of public officials without prior consent
Words reserved exclusively for regulated professions
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Administrative appeal to the President of the Tribunal de Commerce within two months of formal rejection notice

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for manufacturing and commercial entities provided registered address meets legal criteria and no regulatory prohibition applies

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce), Articles L.223-1 to L.223-56 and R.223-1 to R.223-36 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce in the territorial jurisdiction of the registered office, operating through the INPI Guichet Unique (formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Statuts (articles of association) executed as a notarial or private deed, accompanied by Form M0 (déclaration de constitution régulière d'une personne morale) submitted through the online Guichet Unique
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No legal minimum capital; the SARL may be incorporated with €1 authorized capital. The subscribed cash capital must be fully paid up and deposited in an escrow account held by a French bank or notary before filing. Non-cash contributions must be valued by a statutory asset auditor (commissaire aux apports) when the value exceeds €30,000.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The sole shareholder adopts the draft Statuts of FR_SARL, including all clauses on share subscription and allocation. The share capital, as set forth in the Statuts, is fully subscribed and the undersigned states its receipt of the funds deposited with the notary escrow account. The registered office is fixed at [ADDRESS], France. Mr./Ms. [NAME], present and accepting, is appointed Gérant for an unlimited term, with full powers to manage, sign, and represent the Company under Articles L.223-18 and L.223-50. The Gérant is authorized to effect the M0 filing through the INPI Guichet Unique, publish the legal notice in an approved legal gazette, and take all steps to obtain the K-bis extract.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Capital Deposit and Share Subscription Attestation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French bank account or notary escrow account (compte bloqué)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the Statuts and capital subscription signed by each shareholder. Transfer at least the minimum paid-up capital in cash to a special escrow account opened in the name of the company in formation. Obtain the block attestation (attestation de blocage des fonds) from the bank, or, if a notary receives funds, obtain the notarial deed of deposit.
required_dossiers: Draft Statuts (signed in as many originals as required)
Shareholder identification documents (passport/national ID and proof of address)
Bank account documentation and wire confirmation
Attestation of funds blocking or notary receipt
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If attestation is rejected due to insufficient KYC or proof of identity, resubmit corrected shareholder documents and/or adjust capital to match available funds; no penalty if corrected within the same calendar month.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal announcements gazette (journal d'annonces légales) authorized in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After signature of the Statuts, prepare the legal announcement (avis de constitution) containing the corporate purpose (manufacture of microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers), company name, legal form SARL, capital amount, registered office, duration, and the identity of the Gérant. Publish in an authorized legal gazette in the department where the registered office is located and obtain the attestation of publication.
required_dossiers: Final signed Statuts
Corporate name availability verification (INPI SIREN or reserved name certificate)
Legal announcement draft
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is rejected for missing or inconsistent capital or name data, file a corrected announcement within four days; if the company name is unavailable, select a new distinctive name and republish accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete the online M0 declaration, attach the signed Statuts, capital attestation, publication attestation, forged signature declaration, and proof of qualification of the registered office. Pay the registry filing fee and clearance fee. Submit the dossier and retain the proof of deposit.
required_dossiers: Form M0 (déclaration de création/reprise)
Certified true copy of final Statuts
Bank blocking attestation or notary deed of deposit
Legal announcement attestation
Proof of registered office authorization (lease, electricity bill, or owner's consent)
Declaration of no conviction and identity proof for the Gérant
Evidence of legal capacity for non-resident shareholders if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a query is raised by the Greffe, provide additional documents through the Guichet Unique messenger within ten days; if the capital attestation lacks certification, obtain a corrected bank attestation; if registered office proof is ambiguous, submit a notarial lease or formal owner consent.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce of the territorial jurisdiction
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The Guichet Unique transmits the application to the authorized commercial registry. The Greffe performs a legal regularity review, assigns the SIREN/SIRET number, registers the SARL, and issues the K-bis extract and RNE registration certificate. The SARL acquires legal personality only upon registration.
required_dossiers: Complete application transmitted by INPI
Proof of payment of taxes and emoluments
Any supplemental documents requested by the Greffe
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If negative verification arises, the Gérant may request deferral or introduce a judicial rectification application before the President of the Commercial Court; correct any irregularity within fifteen days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce; URSSAF; INSEE; DREETS/DREAL for occupational and environmental filings
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After issuance of the K-bis extract, register the Gérant for French social security, contract mandatory business insurance (civil liability and property damage), and, if required, file the label declaration to industry authorities. Ensure that the registered office and statutory information remain current in the RNE and that occupational health and safety inspections are scheduled.
required_dossiers: K-bis extract
Bank pro-forma insurance quote
Gérant identity proof and social security number
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If social security or professional registration fails due to a SIREN or identity discrepancy, obtain an INSEE confirmation and correct the registry data, then re-submit the enrollment application within five working days.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Agence nationale de sécurité du médicament et des produits de santé (ANSM) for IVD device registration; Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL) under the Prefect for installations classées pour la protection de l'environnement (ICPE)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: IVDR Manufacturer Registration under Regulation (EU) 2017/746 and Prefectural ICPE Authorization or Registration (régime d'enregistrement) for hazardous operations

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Direction Régionale de l'Environnement, de l'Aménagement et du Logement (DREAL), regional branch of the Ministère de la Transition Écologique
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: ICPE Registration (Enregistrement) for solvent and flammable liquid handling codes 4330 and 4331; full EIA Report (Étude d'impact) required if annual solvent consumption exceeds the registration threshold; IVD bench-scale production is generally treated as Déclaration or Exempt if below established risk limits.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge must respect the prefectural order: pH 5.5–9.5, chemical oxygen demand ≤ 2000 mg/L unless further reduced by treatment, biochemical oxygen demand ≤ 800 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 600 mg/L. Fugitive volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions must conform to European Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU limits. Hazardous waste must be traceable via BSDA/BSD tracking and disposed by prefect-approved carriers under code de l'environnement.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification by the Departmental Fire and Rescue Service (SDIS) or an approved inspection bureau in accordance with Code du travail occupational egress and prevention rules; structural load inspection by a certified building control office verifying floor loading for heavy analyzers; workplace clearance through occupational medicine services and DREETS labor inspection confirming ventilation, chemical safety, and emergency response adequacy.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Directorate-General of Public Finance (DGFiP), Paris; online portal www.impots.gouv.fr. Customs and indirect tax matters are administrated by the Directorate-General of Customs and Indirect Rights (DGDDI) via www.douane.gouv.fr.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a foreign-owned SARL: (1) incorporate and file the M0 form at the Centre de Formalités des Entreprises (CFE) to obtain SIREN and SIRET numbers; (2) the corporate tax office (Service des Impôts des Entreprises) issues the French intra-community VAT number (numéro intracommunautaire) after VAT registration; (3) a non-resident taxable person without a French establishment must register using the simplified Form 1487-SD and produce a foreign VAT ID; (4) an EORI number is obtained separately from DGDDI for customs formalities; (5) if a non-EU or non-EEA parent has no permanent establishment, a fiscal representative must be appointed for VAT purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: SARL is default-assessed under corporate income tax (impôt sur les sociétés). It may elect, within the first five fiscal years and subject to conditions, to be taxed like a partnership under personal income tax (option IR). A French corporate group may elect fiscal integration (intégration fiscale) for loss offsetting, and VAT grouping (assujetti unique) may be elected. Hybrid mismatch adjustments are imposed under ATAD implementation (Art. 205 quinquies CGI); there is no US-style check-the-box election in France.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: French TVA (taxe sur la valeur ajoutée), implemented under Code Général des Impôts (CGI) Arts. 256 et seq. and harmonized with the EU VAT Directive 2006/112/EC.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 85,000 annual taxable turnover for supplies of goods / EUR 37,500 for supplies of services (CGI Art. 293 B); an upper abatement band applies (EUR 93,500 / EUR 41,250). Mandatory VAT registration is required once the base threshold is exceeded.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: France mandates structured electronic invoicing for B2B transactions under the reform of TVA e-invoicing. Domestic invoices must be exchanged via Chorus Pro or an accredited dematerialization platform (PDP) in the EN 16931 format, with mandatory e-reporting for cross-border supplies. The phased deadlines apply from 2026/2027. There is no physical revenue stamp or general real-time pre-clearance for IVD goods; compliance is enforced through digital transmission, API validation, and online tax e-filing (GIVRE).

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under CGI Art. 262-I to goods physically exported to destinations outside the EU, including IVD analyzers and microfluidic cartridges, provided the supplier holds documented proof of transport out of the EU and a valid customs export declaration has been accepted. Certain related services (freight, loading, international transport) are zero-rated as export-linked services when supplied directly to the exporter. Offshore digital services supplied to non-EU businesses are outside the scope of French TVA when the customer is in a third country.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration (DAU/ENS) accepted by French Customs (DGDDI) with validated Movement Reference Number (MRN)
Through bill of lading / air waybill (or equivalent transport document) proving physical removal of goods from EU customs territory
Inward remittance certificate / SWIFT payment confirmation showing receipt of export proceeds
Commercial invoice and packing list matching the customs value and declared HS classification
Transport evidence (CMR, transit accompanying document, cargo manifest) where applicable
CE certificate of conformity and IVDR technical documentation for automated point-of-care IVD analyzers
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Incomplete documentation or failed proof of physical export causes immediate reversal of the zero rate, recovery of French VAT plus late-interest, and application of negligence or bad-faith penalties (40% / 80% of the VAT due). Fraudulent structuration may lead to criminal liability under CGI Art. 1741 (up to EUR 45,000 fine and 3 years imprisonment) and additional customs penalties under the Code des Douanes. DGFiP audit windows extend up to six years for undisclosed or fraudulent positions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (BdF) and the French Treasury (Direction Générale du Trésor) under the authority of the Ministry of Economy, Finance and Recovery; EU-level coordination with the European Central Bank (ECB) for monetary policy and the European Systemic Risk Board (ESRB) for macroprudential oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France is a full member of the eurozone; the euro is fully convertible for both current and capital account transactions. Profit remittance is unrestricted under EU capital movement rules (Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, Articles 63-66), subject to standard anti-money laundering (AML) and counter-terrorist financing (CTF) verification. No exchange control approval is required for dividend distributions, loan repayments, or repatriation of invested capital, provided the underlying transactions are properly documented and reported to the Banque de France for statistical purposes (balance of payments reporting).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender of export proceeds is imposed in France. Exporters are free to retain foreign currency earnings in domestic or foreign bank accounts. However, all cross-border transactions exceeding €12,500 must be reported to the Banque de France via the 'Déclaration de Transfert de Fonds' (DTF) for statistical and balance-of-payments purposes. The reporting deadline is within 20 business days following the month of the transaction. There is no conversion ratio requirement; companies may hold foreign currency balances or convert them at their discretion.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Crédit Agricole Corporate and Investment Bank

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. French-regulated Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as Qonto, Shine, and Lydia Solutions offer multi-currency accounts and cross-border payment services. However, for a manufacturing entity with significant trade flows and LC requirements, traditional banks remain more robust. EMIs may lack full trade finance capabilities (e.g., issuance of commercial letters of credit) and may have lower transaction limits. Legal constraints: EMIs must be licensed by the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) and are subject to the same AML/CTF obligations as banks. They cannot provide credit or hold client funds as deposits; they are limited to payment services. For capital escrow or large-scale trade settlements, a full-service bank is recommended.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a corporate entity. French banks mandate that at least one director or a legal representative with power of attorney appear in person at a branch for identity verification and to sign the account opening documents. Remote opening is possible for certain banks (e.g., BNP Paribas, Société Générale) via video conferencing, but this is subject to enhanced due diligence and may require notarized documents and apostille. For a SARL with non-resident shareholders, the bank may require the physical presence of the manager (gérant) or a designated representative. In practice, a physical visit to France is strongly advised to expedite the process and avoid delays.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure (e.g., shareholders or counterparties from non-EU high-risk third countries)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Corporate registry extracts (Kbis) for the SARL and all parent entities; (2) Ultimate Beneficial Owner (UBO) declaration with full identity details and source of funds; (3) Audited financial statements for the last 2 years; (4) Business plan and forecast cash flows; (5) Contracts with suppliers and customers to demonstrate legitimate trade; (6) Tax residency certificates and proof of tax compliance; (7) Detailed explanation of the IVD manufacturing business and regulatory licenses (e.g., CE marking, ISO 13485).

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual transaction patterns (e.g., large cash deposits, rapid in-out flows, or transactions with high-risk jurisdictions)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Maintain a comprehensive transaction ledger with supporting invoices, bills of lading, and customs declarations. Provide a written treasury policy outlining expected transaction volumes and counterparties. For any large or unusual transaction, prepare a source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statement. Engage a reputable external auditor to attest to the legitimacy of the flows.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Incomplete or inconsistent corporate documentation (e.g., missing UBO details, outdated statutes)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit a complete and up-to-date corporate dossier: (1) Certified copy of the Articles of Association (statuts) with all amendments; (2) Certificate of incorporation (extrait Kbis) issued within the last 3 months; (3) List of directors and managers with passport copies; (4) Proof of registered office address (utility bill or lease); (5) UBO declaration form (Déclaration de Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filed with the French Trade Registry (RCS).

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Inbound capital injections (shareholder loans or equity contributions) must be routed via SWIFT MT103 or MT202. The payment must include a clear purpose code (e.g., 'Equity injection' or 'Shareholder loan') and reference the SARL's SIREN number. For amounts exceeding €12,500, the bank will require a DTF declaration. The funds must be received in the SARL's designated capital escrow account or operational account. Verification: The bank will request a copy of the shareholder resolution, the bank statement of the sending entity, and a certificate of the source of funds. For non-EU transfers, additional sanctions screening and enhanced due diligence may apply.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 (single customer credit transfer) for direct payments to suppliers; (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) via SWIFT MT700 series for documentary credit transactions; (3) Documentary collections (D/P, D/A) via SWIFT MT400 series. For high-value or recurring payments, the SARL may use the Single Euro Payments Area (SEPA) for euro-denominated transactions within the EU, but for non-EU suppliers, SWIFT is mandatory. The bank will require underlying trade documents (invoice, bill of lading, packing list) for LC issuance. For FX conversion, the bank will execute at the prevailing interbank rate plus a margin; forward contracts can be arranged.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright Forward Contracts (FX Forwards) with a maturity up to 12 months, available from major French banks for EUR/USD, EUR/CNY, and other major pairs.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies with restricted convertibility (e.g., certain emerging market currencies) – permitted under French regulations, subject to underlying exposure verification.
Currency Swaps (FX Swaps) for simultaneous spot and forward transactions, used for liquidity management and rollover of positions.
Options on FX (European-style) for hedging against adverse movements while retaining upside potential – available from tier-1 banks.
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for long-term hedging of both principal and interest flows, particularly for shareholder loans or project financing.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual ordinary shareholders' meeting (AGO) and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporate body - shareholders of the SARL; minutes recorded in the statutory minute book
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months of fiscal year-end; a calendar-year SARL must hold the meeting no later than 30 June
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Any shareholder may petition the Commercial Court to appoint a proxy (mandataire) to convene the meeting; continued failure to approve accounts prevents the deposit of accounts and exposes the gérant to civil liability, judicial strike-off from the RCS, and ultimately judicial dissolution at the request of an interested party

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts (depot des comptes annuels) and management report at the RCS
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés via the INPI Guichet Unique / RNE electronic portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month of AGO approval; in practice no later than 7 months after fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: The court registrar serves a formal notice to regularize within 1 month; if unaddressed, the company is administratively struck off (radiation) from the RCS, losing standing for IVD supply contracts, banking lines, and eligibility for public tenders; any interested third party may further petition for judicial liquidation

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax return (declaration de resultats n.2065-SD with annexes 2050 to 2059)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (DGFiP) via EDI/EFI electronic filing
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Calendar-year fiscal year-end: e-filing due 3 May of the following year; non-calendar fiscal year-end: due within 3 months of the closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 10% of the assessed tax, increased to 40% after formal notice and 80% for fraudulent concealment, plus late-payment interest of 0.2% per calendar month; the gérant is jointly liable for willful non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final settlement of corporate income tax (solde de l'IS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Balance due on 15 May coinciding with the n.2065 filing; advance instalments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% surcharge where instalments already paid are below 90% of the final corporate income tax due; 5% late-payment penalty and 0.2% monthly interest on the unpaid balance; enforceable distraint against corporate assets

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: VAT returns and payment (CA3 monthly; CA12 and interim instalments under the simplified real regime)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly CA3 filed by the 24th of the following month electronically; under the simplified real regime, interim instalments due 15 July and 15 December and the annual CA12 with balance due by 3 May of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of the VAT due if filed within 30 days, 10% thereafter, and 40% after formal notice for abusive conduct, plus 0.2% monthly interest; electronic filing obligations also require an auditable FEC export trail for the whole accounting year

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Business property contribution (Cotisation Fonciere des Entreprises - CFE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DDFiP local tax office of the municipality where the factory, warehouse, and registered office are physically located
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual payment due 15 December based on the cadastral rental value of business premises; a minimum contribution applies when annual turnover exceeds EUR 500,000
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% deficiency penalty, 0.2% monthly interest, and an enforceable writ after 30 days of non-payment; habitual defaults may trigger administrative seizure of manufacturing equipment and loss of export certificates requiring a tax clearance certificate

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: UBO declaration update (declaration des beneficiaires effectifs)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI Guichet Unique (RCS/RNE file of the SARL)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership or shareholding structure; no separate yearly filing is due when no change occurs during the year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Criminal penalties under Monetary and Financial Code art. L.561-48: 6 months' imprisonment and EUR 6,000 fine for individuals; EUR 30,000 fine for the legal entity; inaccurate UBO data also exposes the IVD distributor chain to enhanced due-diligence scrutiny by financial institutions

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of registry data accuracy at the RNE (justification de l'exactitude des informations)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: INPI / Guichet Unique (Registre National des Entreprises electronic portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once per calendar year, performed concurrently with the annual accounts deposit or through a dedicated no-change declaration before the anniversary of RCS registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to confirm data accuracy allows the registrar to serve two successive formal notices and then strike the SARL off the RCS; knowingly false declarations expose the gérant to criminal penalties for forgery

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual company vehicle tax (taxe annuelle sur les vehicules de societes) for passenger cars registered to the SARL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed and paid by 15 January for vehicles held or leased by the SARL during the preceding calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing penalty plus 0.2% monthly interest on the tax; the gérant is personally liable jointly with the corporate vehicle fleet and penalties are not tax deductible

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Statutory audit (commissaire aux comptes) is mandatory for the SARL when two of the following three thresholds are exceeded at fiscal year-end: balance-sheet total above EUR 4,000,000; net turnover excluding VAT above EUR 8,000,000; average workforce above 50 employees (Code de commerce arts. L.232-6-1 and R.232-1). In parallel, the IVD manufacturing activity under EU Regulation 2017/746 requires a certified ISO/IEC 13485 quality-management system audited annually by a notified body, which is a regulatory conformity audit distinct from the statutory financial audit.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (Plan Comptable General) as set by the ANC and Code de commerce arts. L.123-12 to L.123-22, transposing EU Directive 2013/34/EU; the SARL prepares individual statutory accounts under the normal real regime and files the standard 2050-series tax liasse; IFRS is optional only for consolidated statutory accounts and is not recommended for a non-listed SARL.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% standard French corporate income tax rate (CGI Art. 219); reduced rate of 15% applies to qualifying SMEs on the first EUR 42,000 of taxable profit per fiscal year.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME reduced CT rate: 15% on first EUR 42,000 of profit; Crédit d'Impôt Recherche (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenditure up to EUR 100 million; Crédit d'Impôt Innovation at 25% of eligible innovation expenditure capped at EUR 400,000 for SMEs; JEI (young innovative company) exemption for qualifying R&D-intensive SMEs.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite (no time limit) under CGI Art. 209, subject to statutory annual utilization cap of EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income exceeding EUR 1,000,000; carryback available for only one year up to EUR 1,000,000.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 2065-SD (liasse fiscale: 2050 to 2059-SD annexes) filed electronically through the EDI-TDFC/EFI system on impots.gouv.fr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; quarterly advance corporate income tax prepayments due 15 March, 15 June, 15 September and 15 December based on prior-year assessed tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a calendar-year company, the annual return is due by the second working day after 1 May (e.g., 5 May 2025); for an off-calendar fiscal year, within three months of the accounting year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: SIREN, SIRET, APE/NAF code, legal form (SARL), registered office, accounting reference period, French tax residence data.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A French SARL is fiscally resident in France if its effective place of management is in France; report worldwide income. Foreign shareholders do not alter the entity's residence.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report total taxable turnover, including French sales and exports of IVD instruments, microfluidic cartridges and immunoassay analyzers, excluding French VAT.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report worldwide invoiced sales; foreign permanent establishment profits are reconciled under applicable double tax treaties, with treaty claims documented in the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report operating profit after deductible expenses; include arm's-length adjustments for cross-border purchases, royalties and management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to related non-residents must be substantiated under CGI Art. 57; payments to tax-haven intermediaries may be disallowed under Art. 238 A.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the balance of prior-year deductible tax losses available for offset in the current fiscal year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A foreign-owned French SARL may claim carried-forward losses; the annual limit is EUR 1,000,000 plus 50% of taxable income above that threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim eligible R&D costs for IVD assay development, clinical validation, engineering and software development embedded in automated point-of-care analyzers.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: CIR is available to the French tax-resident manufacturing company even if foreign-owned, provided eligible R&D is conducted in France/EEA and cost substantiation is retained.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declare controlled transactions with foreign related parties exceeding the statutory threshold; attach supporting transfer pricing documentation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Prepare a local file/master file if group-wide threshold met; ensure distribution policies, IP and intercompany services are documented and priced at arm's length.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: 10% flat increase after formal notice; late payment interest 0.20% per month (2.4% annual); deliberate omission triggers 40% penalty; abusive arrangement rises to 80%; fraudulent declarations are referred to the public prosecutor.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory dividend WHT for non-resident corporate recipients (CGI Art. 119 bis 2); 12.8% for non-resident individuals, subject to treaty reduction and possible 2% solidarity levy for non-EU/EEA residents.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the beneficial owner must obtain a Form 5000 tax residence certificate from its state of residence and provide it to the French paying agent, together with a beneficial-ownership statement, before distribution. The Parent-Subsidiary Directive exemption applies to EU corporate parents with a 10% qualifying holding maintained for two years. If statutory WHT was withheld, a refund claim must be lodged within the statutory deadline, generally by 31 December of the second calendar year following payment.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic non-treaty rates: 25% WHT on royalties and 25% WHT on interest paid to non-residents. Treaty rates commonly reduce dividends, interest and royalties to 0%, 5%, 10% or 15% depending on beneficial ownership and treaty terms; intra-EU associates may qualify for 0% WHT under the EU Interest & Royalties Directive.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Full OECD-style Master File/Local File mandatory when group-wide gross turnover or gross assets reach EUR 400,000,000 (CGI Art. L.13 AA/L.13 AB; BOFIP conditions); annual controlled-transaction declaration on Form 2257-SD is triggered when foreign related-party transactions exceed EUR 100,000.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France has no standalone ESR regime, but applies a substantive fiscal-residence test (CGI Art. 209: place of effective management in France), the judicial abuse-of-law doctrine (LPF Art. L.64), the OECD Principal Purpose Test, and anti-artificial-scheme rules. A French SARL must maintain genuine local premises, staff, board minutes, bank accounts, operational decision-making and physical substance; a shell with sham management in an offshore jurisdiction risks treaty denial, 80% penalties and criminal tax fraud referral.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of taxable revenue, false IVD export invoicing, fabrication of fake intercompany transactions, destruction of accounting records, or undisclosed offshore bank accounts.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Imprisonment up to 5 years and fine up to EUR 500,000 (CGI Art. 1741); aggravated fraud using fictitious entities or offshore accounts: 7 years imprisonment and EUR 3,000,000 fine; tax reassessment with 40% intentional-misstatement penalty or 80% fraudulent-abuse penalty plus 0.20% monthly late interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The SARL gérant may be criminally convicted, personally ordered to pay all evaded taxes and penalties, banned from managing, subjected to travel restrictions, and in insolvency held liable for corporate debts under Art. L.223-22 Code de commerce where managerial fault caused the shortfall.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer Pricing Abuse / Hidden Profit Shifting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Non-arm's-length pricing on microfluidic cartridges, immunoassay analyzers, IP royalties, technical service fees, or deliberate absence of Master File/Local File after statutory threshold is exceeded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax redetermination of profits to arm's length; denial of deductibility for tax-haven payments under Art. 238 A CGI; 40% penalty for deliberate transfer-pricing misstatement; 80% penalty for abusive transfer to a related entity in a preferential tax regime plus late payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly sign false documentation or orchestrate sham intercompany contracts may be joint debtors for corporate tax and penalties, face criminal tax evasion charges, and be disqualified from management.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: French registered address used only for mail collection, no employees, no business premises, no genuine board decisions in France, and center of economic activities located abroad while treaty benefits are claimed through the French SARL.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Abuse-of-law procedure under LPF Art. L.64; the SARL is disregarded, taxable income is attributed to the true beneficial owner, 80% penalty is imposed on redirected profits, and mandatory referral to the criminal prosecutor occurs for abuse of law.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Piercing of the corporate veil is available in cases of fictitious management or grave misconduct; the manager and real beneficial owners may be jointly and severally liable for corporate debts, subject to civil restitution, travel bans, and imprisonment for tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Abusive Treaty/Directive Relief and Beneficial-Ownership Misrepresentation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Inserting a conduit entity, backdating beneficial-ownership declarations, or using fabricated tax residence certificates to obtain 0% Parent-Subsidiary Directive relief or reduced treaty WHT on dividends, interest or royalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Denial of treaty or EU directive relief; retroactive reinstatement of 25% statutory WHT; 80% abusive-arrangement penalty; potential withholding-tax evasion prosecution under Art. 1741 CGI and monetary penalties under the French Monetary and Financial Code.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Signing officers who issue or present false TRC/beneficial-ownership certificates are personally liable for resulting tax deficiencies and penalties, may face criminal prosecution for forgery and tax fraud, and may be subject to imprisonment and prohibition from corporate management.
